sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Springe, at the foot of the Deister, says it charges no parking fees, and the live question is whether that will change. The town's marketing page states that Springe charges no parking fees and that free parking is available under parking-disc rules [1]. On 20 October 2026 the town announced a new parking map showing seven designated car parks in the direct city centre, where parking is usually free but time-limited, mostly to one or two hours [0]. The town's 2025 brochure lists a parking guidance scheme with seven numbered car parks, among them the Parkpalette at Nordwall [2]. A budget crisis may end the free parking. An external consultant's report of 16 April 2026 lists introducing parking fees as a budget measure and, assuming about 1,471 candidate spaces, 50 percent use, 0.50 euro an hour and a ten-hour maximum, estimates about 783,000 euros a year, excluding park-and-ride; this is a revenue estimate and not a decided tariff [5]. The report says the council had partly spoken against charging at park-and-ride sites, while the consultant saw no objection in principle, and that a camera-supported system at the Parkpalette is being examined, with a test phase possible after a council decision [6]. In the council's traffic-light vote on consolidation measures, presented on 9 January 2025, the parking-fee measure got grade 1 from 16 members, grade 2 from 11 and grade 3 from 2, and measures with a majority of grade 1 are to be developed to decision readiness [7]. We found no tariff statute and no per-car-park disc limits.

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development is the new central bus station. A council paper of 21 May 2026 on Bebauungsplan Nr. 88 says the redesign removes the 73 existing park-and-ride spaces at Springe station, which the town expects to be absorbed by parking along Bahnhofstraße, the Jägerallee park-and-ride site, described as little used, 14 new car spaces and an extension of the eastern park-and-ride area [10]. The council adopted the plan as a bylaw on 25 June 2026, with 31 yes votes, no no votes and 1 abstention, and the Region Hannover is preparing the bus station redesign [11]. The town's urban development concept of October 2023 calls parking in the core town generally sufficient, with many short-stay spaces behind the main streets, notes heavy morning search traffic near the vocational school, and says the new town hall on the Burghof will remove many spaces students use [3]. It also calls the parking guidance system outdated and proposes renewing it, at an estimated 20,000 euros for a concept and 300,000 euros for implementation; we found no funding or implementation decision [4]. The Stadtwerke run nine public charging posts, six in the core town and three in the districts [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Deutsche Bahn lists an open P+R at Bürgermeister-Peters-Straße at Springe station with 60 spaces, round the clock, which the town describes as free [12]. It lists 289 spaces at P+R Völksen, for the Völksen-Eldagsen station, where a Region release of May 2021 named 233, and the two figures are unreconciled; our feed gives 222 [13]. The Region Hannover says its area has about 6,100 park-and-ride spaces, all free to use [15]. In 2021 the Region installed sensors at five pilot park-and-ride sites, including Völksen/Eldagsen, with occupancy published online [14].

Our data cover the Völksen/Eldagsen park-and-ride, whose feed gives 222 spaces, so the percentages are approximate. Over about 27 days since late September 2026 occupancy averaged about 19% on weekdays and 8% at weekends, with a peak of 49% on a Tuesday morning, which fits a commuter car park. The centre's seven car parks are not in our data.
